metadata.title: Why splitting a chunk from its document makes it retrieve for the wrong question
metadata.purpose: Redo of the claude-basics reel in the hai-simple form: a hesitant-writer cold open, Plain register, Liam narrating, Humanitarians AI outro. Same facts and argument as the source — a chunk cut from its document loses the context that resolves ambiguous token matches; prepending a short document-level summary before embedding restores it.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro am_onyx) — master clock; conform each beat to measured audio
metadata.exclusions: chunking strategies, embedding-model comparisons, full-pipeline benchmarking
metadata.anchor_pair: S01 -> S05 (the medical-paper chunk, same case)

beats.narration_text: You might think a chunk retrieves badly because it got shrunk too small. It isn't size — it's this: why does splitting a chunk from its document make it retrieve for the wrong question?

props.text:
Why does shrinking a chunk
make it retrieve
for the wrong question?

beats.narration_text: A medical paper is split into twenty chunks for search. Chunk seven reads: "This treatment reduced mortality by twelve percent" — with no disease named anywhere in it.

items.label: A medical paper is split into twenty chunks
items.sub: A medical paper is split into twenty chunks for search.

items.label: Chunk 7: "reduced mortality by 12%" —
items.sub: Chunk seven reads: "This treatment reduced mortality by twelve percent" — with no disease named anywhere in it.

beats.narration_text: The natural assumption is that search matches on words, so a chunk about "mortality" should surface for any mortality question, right disease or not.

items.label: Search matches on words —
items.sub: The natural assumption is that search matches on words,

items.label: so "mortality" finds any mortality question
items.sub: so a chunk about "mortality" should surface for any mortality question, right disease or not.

beats.narration_text: A word-matching search hands that chunk to a "diabetes mortality" query on the word match alone — it has nothing to do with diabetes, but nothing in the chunk says so.

items.label: Hands the chunk to "diabetes mortality" —
items.sub: A word-matching search hands that chunk to a "diabetes mortality" query on the word match alone —

items.label: nothing in the chunk says otherwise
items.sub: it has nothing to do with diabetes, but nothing in the chunk says so.

beats.narration_text: The fix: generate a short summary of the whole document, and prepend it to the chunk before embedding. The vector then carries the chunk's own words plus its place in the document, so an ambiguous phrase resolves against real context.

items.label: Summarize the document, prepend it to the chunk
items.sub: The fix: generate a short summary of the whole document, and prepend it to the chunk before embedding.

items.label: The vector now carries content plus place
items.sub: The vector then carries the chunk's own words plus its place in the document, so an ambiguous phrase resolves against real context.

beats.narration_text: Prepend "Context: hypertension study in elderly patients" to chunk seven, and it stops matching diabetes queries. Across ten test queries, precision on that chunk moved from thirty-three percent to ninety.

items.label: "Context: hypertension study" — stops matching diabetes
items.sub: Prepend "Context: hypertension study in elderly patients" to chunk seven, and it stops matching diabetes queries.

items.label: Precision: 33% -> 90%
items.sub: Across ten test queries, precision on that chunk moved from thirty-three percent to ninety.

beats.narration_text: That gain only shows up if the chunk was ambiguous to begin with — a chunk that already names its subject gets nothing from the extra context.

props.title: ONLY WHEN THE CHUNK WAS AMBIGUOUS

items.label: The gain needs an ambiguous chunk
items.sub: That gain only shows up if the chunk was ambiguous to begin with —

items.label: a chunk that already names its subject gains nothing
items.sub: a chunk that already names its subject gets nothing from the extra context.

beats.narration_text: And it doesn't fix a document summarized badly, or a search built on a broken chunking strategy in the first place — this repairs one specific failure, not retrieval in general.

props.title: ONE FAILURE, NOT ALL OF RETRIEVAL

items.label: Doesn't fix a bad summary or broken chunking
items.sub: And it doesn't fix a document summarized badly, or a search built on a broken chunking strategy in the first place —

items.label: this repairs one specific failure
items.sub: this repairs one specific failure, not retrieval in general.

beats.narration_text: A chunk answers the question inside it. Prepending its document's context is what lets it also answer the right question.

props.quote: A chunk answers the question inside it. Prepending its document's context is what lets it also answer the right question.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I have a research paper being split into chunks for RAG. A chunk says "This treatment reduced mortality by twelve percent" with no disease name in context. Show me how to prepend a context header to each chunk before embedding, what fields belong in that header, and how I'd verify the fix is actually preventing false matches on unrelated queries.
